findings.title: Options-object default makes clearQueue reject pending work by default
findings.cause: The options destructuring now defaults rejectOnClear to true at index.js:7, while clearQueue rejects every queued item whenever rejectOnClear is true.
findings.impact: Callers using the documented pLimit({concurrency: 1}) form get AbortError rejections from clearQueue even though the public default is false. This can break teardown code and produce unexpected or unhandled rejections.
findings.evidence: readme.md:48-49 documents rejectOnClear as boolean default false. index.js:7 sets the default to true. index.js:84-88 rejects queued promises when enabled. The focused runtime probe returned defaultClearQueue: rejected:AbortError for pLimit({concurrency: 1}).
findings.reproduction_or_test: Create pLimit({concurrency: 1}), enqueue one running task and one pending task, await one tick, call clearQueue(), then race the pending promise with a timer. Expected default behavior is still-pending; current behavior rejects with AbortError.

findings.title: Falsey non-boolean rejectOnClear options bypass runtime validation
findings.cause: The runtime type check at index.js:12 only runs when rejectOnClear is truthy, so values such as 0, null, or an empty string are accepted.
findings.impact: Invalid caller configuration is silently accepted despite the boolean-only runtime contract, creating inconsistent behavior between types, docs, and runtime validation.
findings.evidence: readme.md:48 says rejectOnClear has type boolean. index.test-d.ts:29 expects a non-boolean rejectOnClear to be rejected at the type level. The focused runtime probe returned rejectOnClearZero: accepted for pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0}).
findings.reproduction_or_test: Assert that pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0}) throws TypeError. Current code accepts it because 0 is falsey.

findings.title: limit.map drops the index for non-array iterables
findings.cause: index.js:108 checks Array.isArray(iterable) and index.js:111 passes undefined instead of the Array.from index for Set, generator, and iterator inputs.
findings.impact: Mappers that depend on the documented index argument work for arrays but break for other supported iterables, even though limit.map explicitly accepts any iterable.
findings.evidence: readme.md:82-84 says the mapper receives item value and index and is equivalent to Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => limit(mapperFunction, item, index)). index.d.ts:32-33 covers Set and iterator inputs. The focused runtime probe returned mapSetIndexes: ["a:undefined", "b:undefined"].
findings.reproduction_or_test: await pLimit(1).map(new Set(['a', 'b']), (value, index) => `${value}:${String(index)}`) should produce ["a:0", "b:1"], but currently produces ["a:undefined", "b:undefined"].

findings.title: limitFunction ignores caller arguments
findings.cause: index.js:124 returns a zero-argument wrapper and calls function_() without forwarding the wrapper's arguments.
findings.impact: The named helper is unusable for functions that require inputs. Documented patterns such as limitedFetchUrl(url) call the wrapped function with undefined instead of the provided URL.
findings.evidence: index.d.ts:25-26 types the returned limited function as accepting the original function's arguments. recipes.md:161-163 demonstrates limitedFetchUrl(url). The focused runtime probe returned limitFunctionArgs: undefined:undefined for a wrapper called as limited('x', 'y').
findings.reproduction_or_test: const limited = limitFunction((a, b) => `${a}:${b}`, {concurrency: 1}); await limited('x', 'y') should resolve to x:y, but currently resolves to undefined:undefined.

findings.title: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY concurrency is rejected
findings.cause: index.js:128 now requires Number.isInteger(concurrency), removing the previous explicit allowance for concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY.
findings.impact: Consumers using Infinity as an unbounded concurrency mode get a TypeError, which is a backward-incompatible runtime regression from the committed implementation.
findings.evidence: git diff -- index.js shows the removed Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY branch in validateConcurrency. The focused runtime probe returned infinityConcurrency: rejected:Expected `concurrency` to be a number from 1 and up.
findings.reproduction_or_test: pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) should construct a limiter as in the committed implementation, but currently throws TypeError.
